Operative text: BPU standards define a large data center with a minimum megawatt designation not greater than 50 MW. Chapter number confirmed by the text header and fastdemocracy.com bill page.

territorial_scope.description: Applies to electric public utilities and large data center customers in New Jersey, within each utility's service area.

evidence.quote: within the electric public utility’s service area

summary.short: Requires New Jersey electric public utilities to seek Board of Public Utilities approval of a rate class and tariff for large data center customers, so that other customers do not subsidize their costs. Customers must post financial guarantees and accept curtailment and flexibility duties. Takes effect immediately.
summary.long: Supplements Title 48 to regulate retail electricity service to large data centers in New Jersey. Within 12 months, the Board of Public Utilities must set by order standards for each electric public utility, including defining characteristics of a large data center (minimum size not greater than 50 megawatts, with commonly owned or co-located facilities aggregated). The standards aim to keep other customers from subsidizing data center costs and from bearing stranded costs. They also cover co-located generation, capacity valuation, load-forecast submissions, a voluntary demand-reduction program, interconnection and curtailment priority (data centers before residential customers, excluding designated critical load), and anti-evasion measures. Within 180 days after that order, each utility must petition for a rate class and tariff, which the Board approves if it meets the Act. Large data center customers must provide financial guarantees for at least 85 percent of their electricity supply over 10 years, post deposits or security, accept demand-flexibility commitments, report flexibility performance annually, and pay interconnection study costs. Facilities approved before enactment are exempt from some of these duties for their already approved megawatts. Rate and service agreements must meet the Act's protections, and FERC jurisdiction over wholesale sales and transmission is preserved. The Act takes effect immediately.

notes: Reprint format: bracketed text marks struck language and ^ markers mark amendments, so the annotator coded the unbracketed text as operative. The bracketed old section 1 contains a 100 megawatt data center definition and an 85 percent guarantee; the new section 1 instead leaves the size threshold to Board standards capped at 50 megawatts. The registry bill number S731 does not appear in the document, which identifies the act as Assembly No. 796 (Fourth Reprint). No enabling act is stated. Missing registry IDs are left as empty strings.

“Electric public utility” means the same as the term is defined in section 3 of P.L.1999, c.23 (C.48:3-51)
“Large data center” means a data center that meets the size threshold and other defining characteristics established by the board
“Large data center customer” means a customer of an electric public utility responsible for one or more large data centers
“Co-located generation” means an electric power generation facility that is interconnected directly with a data center customer’s electrical load
“Capacity resource” means an energy resource, including generation, energy storage, demand response, demand reduction, energy efficiency, or any combination thereof
“Demand flexibility” means the ability of a customer to modify the timing, level, or pattern of their electricity consumption in response to grid conditions

obligations.summary: Rates, terms and conditions the Board approves for large data center customers must reasonably protect other utility customers against increased transmission and distribution costs; the Board must require each electric public utility to impose the protections listed in paragraphs (1) to (10).

enforcement.note: The Act sets no fines, criminal penalties, licence revocation, clawback, suspension or blocking. Subsection d(5)(b) mentions financial penalties for non-performance of demand flexibility commitments, but leaves them to the tariff. This text states no amount, formula, authority or cure period for them, so no enforcement row is coded.
